critical_steps: Inverse difference B with root evaluation and edge increments gives Q=B*B with one-unit root grounding.
Orthonormal radial and sibling-contrast invariant subspaces exhaust dimension 1+...+b^h and yield T_{b,ell} multiplicities.
Jacobi three-term recurrence gives the stated Chebyshev characteristic equation.
Strict positivity of Q inverse and Perron eigenvector places smallest eigenvalue in radial block; leaf-backward recurrence gives positivity of all input increments.
Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz resistance lower bound and matching radial trial upper bound give the explicit b-dependent asymptotic.
Path b=1 handled separately by exact tridiagonal sine spectrum.
claim_to_evidence.domain: Integers b>=2,h>=1; complete depth-h b-ary rooted tree; counting ell2 on every vertex and root-inclusive ancestor sum, real or complex scalars.
claim_to_evidence.unproved_limits: No claims for weighted vertex measures or irregular trees, no uniformity in b as h grows, and no independent literature exhaustive-coverage proof.

correctness.rationale: Exact inverse B, positive grounded quadratic form, orthogonal radial/contrast Jacobi decomposition with dimension check, Chebyshev determinant, Perron simple radial extremizer, and matching Cauchy-Schwarz/trial-profile asymptotic. Finite computations are not treated as infinite proofs.

The standard graph Laplacian of a rooted b-ary tree has root diagonal b and zero eigenvalue; the studied B*B has root diagonal b+1 and is strictly positive definite.
Rojo–Soto 2005, The spectra of the adjacency matrix and Laplacian matrix for some balanced trees, abstract: tridiagonal blocks for standard adjacency and Laplacian.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest published tridiagonal theory treats tree adjacency and graph Laplacian. Direct substitution of its standard Laplacian spectrum cannot yield the present spectrum: the grounding term at the root changes the radial block, removes the null mode, and determines a nontrivial exponentially small eigenvalue. The same representation technique is related, but the accessible statements do not dominate the grounded operator claim, especially the exact norm asymptotic. The full 2007 manuscript was inaccessible, so the possibility of a more general boundary-perturbation theorem is a material documented risk.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A general tree Hardy trace condition yields boundedness criteria but no equation for each finite singular value. Continuous-tree approximation results do not evaluate the unweighted finite vertex spectrum. Ordinary Laplacian tridiagonal results describe a different matrix and contain a zero mode absent here. While symmetry methods can be adapted, the inspected statements and abstracts do not themselves imply the claimed grounded Jacobi equation or fixed-b branching coefficient. The unresolved full text of the 2007 comparator is retained as a risk, not silently labeled NOT_COVERING.

value.rationale: Exact complete singular values of a natural tree Hardy integral simultaneously determine sharp Hilbert embedding constants and all finite-rank approximation errors. The fixed-branching exponential constant and contrasting exact path formula explain the functional-analytic effect of branching, rather than merely evaluating a small arbitrary matrix. The result is self-contained and applies to every b and depth under its declared measure.
